lesson_title: Queue or Side by Side? Two Ways to Join Cells
hook_text: Put a cell in your remote the wrong way and it stops working. Here is the maths of joining cells.
clip_script: Join torch cells end to end, positive to negative, and you have cells in series. Each bit of charge gets a push from every cell, so the voltages add. One cell, 1,5 volts. Two, 3 volts. Three, 4,5 volts. The bulb gets brighter with each one. But flip one cell around and it pushes backwards, cancelling one of the others. That is why your remote dies when a cell is in the wrong way. Now join cells side by side, all the positives together and all the negatives together. That is parallel. Each bit of charge only goes through one cell, so the voltage stays at 1,5 volts and the bulb is no brighter. The bonus? The cells share the work, so the bulb lasts about twice as long. Backup batteries for load shedding use both: series for more volts, parallel for more hours.
visual_style: Cells clicking into a torch end to end with a voltage counter climbing; a reversed cell flashing red; cells side by side with a battery-life bar stretching; a home backup battery bank.
pacing: Everyday hook, a counting rhythm for series, a pause for the reversed cell, then the parallel twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw both circuits with the right symbols.
